subject: ss-pulmonology
title: Mediastinal masses by compartment with diaphragm disorders and paralysis
refs: ITMIS thymoma guidance and WHO 2021 thoracic tumours classification

steps.tx: The **mediastinum** (the space between the lungs holding heart, great vessels and airways) splits into **superior**, **anterior**, **middle** and **posterior** compartments. A mass location narrows the differential sharply on the first chest film. **Four Ts** (thymic, thyroid, teratoma, terrible lymphoma) dominate anterior lesions.
steps.say: The mediastinum is the space between the lungs and it splits into superior, anterior, middle and posterior compartments. Location is the first filter before any scan. Anterior masses follow the four Ts rule, thymic, thyroid, teratoma and lymphoma, which is the single most examined shortcut in this topic.

steps.tx: **Thymoma** (epithelial tumour of thymic remnants) is the commonest anterior mass in adults and links with **myasthenia gravis** in about **thirty** to **fifty** percent of cases. It grows silently and can invade pleura and pericardium. **Paraneoplastic** clues include red cell aplasia and Cushing syndrome.
steps.say: Thymoma is the commonest adult anterior mediastinal tumour and about a third to a half of patients have myasthenia gravis. It grows slowly and invades pleura and pericardium. Paraneoplastic red cell aplasia and Cushing syndrome are rare but classic exam associations.

steps.tx: **Hodgkin lymphoma** (Reed Sternberg cell disease) favours the anterior mediastinum in young women as nodular sclerosis type, causing **superior vena cava obstruction** and cough. Germ cell tumours arise from yolk sac elements and secrete **alpha fetoprotein** (AFP) and **beta human chorionic gonadotropin** (beta HCG). Markers separate malignant germ cell tumours from seminoma patterns.
steps.say: Hodgkin lymphoma in the anterior mediastinum classically affects young women and blocks the superior vena cava. Germ cell tumours secrete alpha fetoprotein and beta human chorionic gonadotropin, and those markers guide typing and follow up. Marker status guides chemotherapy and surveillance decisions.

steps.tx: **Neurogenic tumours** (nerve or ganglia origin) occupy the posterior compartment and include **schwannoma**, **paraganglioma** and ganglion cell tumours. They often grow inside the spinal canal as **dumbbell** lesions. **Horner syndrome** (ptosis, miosis, anhydrosis) and rib erosion point to apical paravertebral lesions.
steps.say: Neurogenic tumours live in the posterior mediastinum and dumbbell lesions grow into the spinal canal. Horner syndrome and rib erosion suggest an apical lesion. Magnetic resonance imaging of the spine is mandatory before any resection approach is chosen.

steps.tx: **Superior vena cava syndrome** (facial swelling, distended neck veins, collateral flow) arises from lymphoma, lung cancer and thymic invasion. **Computed tomography** (CT) with contrast is the first test and shows fat planes, vascular encasement and invasion. **Magnetic resonance imaging** (MRI) adds cardiac and chest wall detail when CT is equivocal.
steps.say: Superior vena cava syndrome means facial swelling with distended neck veins and collateral flow. Contrast computed tomography is the first investigation and shows encasement and invasion. Magnetic resonance imaging adds cardiac and chest wall detail when the computed tomography answer is unclear.

steps.tx: Tissue diagnosis uses **endobronchial ultrasound** (EBUS) for nodal and central lesions, **image guided core biopsy** for anterior masses and **mediastinoscopy** when smaller samples fail. **Pulmonary function tests** (PFTs) and cardiac assessment precede resection, since post operative ventilation and arrhythmia risk decide fitness. Old fashioned needle aspiration alone rarely suffices for typing.
steps.say: Endobronchial ultrasound and image guided core biopsy get tissue for most lesions, and mediastinoscopy backs them up when samples fail. Lung function and cardiac tests decide resectability. Simple needle aspiration alone rarely types these tumours adequately, so core tissue is the standard.

steps.tx: Resectable **thymoma** and encapsulated **teratoma** suit complete surgical excision after neoadjuvant therapy for invasive disease. **Lymphoma** and malignant **germ cell** tumours receive chemotherapy first and surgery rarely helps. Surgical access uses **video assisted thoracoscopic surgery** (VATS), sternotomy or robotic approaches by compartment.
steps.say: Resectable thymoma and teratoma need complete surgical excision, while lymphoma and malignant germ cell tumours get chemotherapy first. Surgery rarely cures lymphoma. The operative route, thoracoscopic, sternotomy or robotic, follows the compartment and the expected invasion.

steps.tx: **Diaphragmatic paralysis** (phrenic nerve failure) raises one hemidiaphragm and leaves orthopnoea and basal collapse on that side. **Sniff test** under fluoroscopy shows paradoxical upward motion of the paralysed side during inspiration. **Diaphragmatic eventration** (congenital thinning) mimics paralysis on films but paradoxical motion is absent.
steps.say: Diaphragmatic paralysis raises one side and causes orthopnoea with basal collapse. The sniff test under fluoroscopy shows paradoxical upward motion. Eventration looks similar on a static film but the paradoxical motion is missing, so imaging distinguishes them.

steps.tx: **Phrenic nerve** injury follows trauma, neck surgery and tumour invasion closely, and bilateral failure causes frank **respiratory failure** with ventilatory dependence in many patients. **Diaphragm plication** (surgical flattening) relieves dyspnoea in symptomatic unilateral paralysis. Electromyography and **phrenic nerve conduction** studies confirm chronic denervation before the operation.
steps.say: Phrenic nerve injury follows trauma, neck surgery or tumour invasion, and bilateral failure causes respiratory failure. Plication improves breathlessness and helps symptomatic cases. Nerve conduction studies confirm chronic denervation before the surgeon commits.

steps.tx: High yield for the exam: the compartment rule decides the diagnosis, thymoma links with **myasthenia gravis**, posterior neurogenic tumours risk dumbbell spread, contrast CT comes first, PET CT stages lymphoma, core biopsy beats aspiration, chemotherapy leads for lymphoma, and the **sniff test** separates paralysis from eventration.
steps.say: Compartment decides the diagnosis, thymoma links with myasthenia, neurogenic tumours risk dumbbell spread, contrast tomography comes first, positron emission tomography stages lymphoma, core biopsy beats aspiration, chemotherapy leads for lymphoma, and the sniff test separates paralysis from eventration.
